meta.name: Tartine Rugelach
meta.total_time: ~2 hrs (40 min active, 1 hr chill, 12 min freeze, 22 min bake)
meta.description: Flaky cream cheese dough rolled into 16 crescents around a walnut-currant-cinnamon filling. Tartine baker Davita's version uses part einkorn flour for lighter, flakier layers and a higher rise than all-AP versions.

vessels.name: Stand Mixer Bowl
vessels.reuse: Used only for cream cheese dough — wash and dry after dough is shaped into disc.

vessels.name: Food Processor
vessels.reuse: Used only for walnut-currant filling — pulse walnuts, then sugar + cinnamon, then transfer filling to a bowl for stirring in currants.

vessels.name: Baking Sheet
vessels.reuse: Lined with parchment — used for shaping placement, freezer chill, and bake.

states.title: Beat Cream Cheese
states.direction: In stand mixer bowl fitted with paddle attachment, beat the softened cream cheese on medium speed for 5 minutes to soften and aerate slightly.
states.exit_condition: Cream cheese is smooth, lightened in color, and slightly aerated — no visible lumps or hard chunks.

notes.text: Cream cheese must be at true room temperature (~68°F/20°C). Cold cream cheese will not aerate; the dough will be lumpy.

states.title: Add Softened Butter
states.direction: Add the softened butter and mix on medium speed until smooth, 1 to 2 minutes, stopping the mixer to scrape down the sides of the bowl a few times.
states.exit_condition: Cream cheese and butter are fully combined into a smooth, homogeneous mixture with no streaks of butter visible.

states.title: Add Flours and Salt
states.direction: Add both flours and the salt. Mix on medium speed until the dough just comes together and begins to ball around the paddle. Do not overmix.
states.exit_condition: Dough balls around the paddle but is moist with some chunks and visible specks of loose flour. Not totally cohesive — that's correct.

notes.text: Undermixing is the goal. Overmixed dough develops gluten and loses flakiness. Specks of loose flour should still be visible.

states.title: Shape Dough Disc
states.direction: Turn the dough out onto a sheet of plastic wrap and form a 2.5cm thick disc. Wrap tightly.
states.exit_condition: Dough is a flat disc roughly 2.5cm thick, tightly wrapped in plastic with no exposed dough.

states.title: Chill Dough
states.direction: Refrigerate the wrapped dough for at least 1 hour, or overnight.
states.exit_condition: Dough is firm and cold throughout, no longer tacky. Easy to roll without sticking excessively.

notes.text: Overnight chill is fine and often improves both flavor and roll-out behavior — dough relaxes and rolls more evenly.

reminders.prompt: Dough texture out of fridge — too firm, just right, or still soft?

states.title: Pulse Walnuts
states.direction: In food processor fitted with the steel blade, pulse the walnuts until the pieces are small — about the size of sunflower seeds.
states.exit_condition: Walnut pieces are roughly sunflower-seed sized — uniform pieces, not powdered, no whole halves remaining.

notes.text: Over-processing turns walnuts into nut butter. Stop when most pieces are small but a few are still slightly larger.

states.title: Add Brown Sugar and Cinnamon
states.direction: Add the brown sugar and ground cinnamon to the processor. Pulse again to combine.
states.exit_condition: Sugar, cinnamon, and walnut pieces are evenly mixed — uniform light brown color throughout, no streaks of plain sugar.

states.title: Stir in Currants
states.direction: Transfer the walnut-sugar mixture to a medium bowl. Stir in the currants by hand — do not pulse.
states.exit_condition: Currants are evenly distributed throughout the filling but remain whole. Filling is ready to spread.

states.title: Preheat Oven
states.direction: Adjust oven rack to middle position. Preheat oven to 350°F (180°C). Line the baking sheet with parchment paper or a nonstick liner.
states.exit_condition: Oven is fully preheated to 350°F (180°C) and the baking sheet is lined and ready.

states.title: Roll Dough to 28cm Circle
states.direction: Lightly dust your work surface with flour and turn the chilled dough out onto it. Using a rolling pin, roll out the dough to form a circle 28cm in diameter and a little thicker than 3mm.
states.exit_condition: Dough is a 28cm round, evenly thick at slightly over 3mm. Edges may be ragged — that's fine.

notes.text: If the dough cracks or feels too firm to roll, let it rest at room temperature 5-10 minutes before rolling.

states.title: Brush with Melted Butter
states.direction: Very lightly brush the rolled dough surface with the melted, cooled butter.
states.exit_condition: Entire dough surface has a thin, even layer of melted butter — not pooling or saturated.

states.title: Spread Walnut-Currant Filling
states.direction: Spread a thick layer of the walnut-currant filling over the buttered dough, equal in thickness to the dough. Leave a 12mm border around the edge.
states.exit_condition: Filling covers the dough in an even layer roughly 3mm thick, with a clean 12mm border at the edge.

states.title: Cut into 16 Triangles
states.direction: With a pizza cutter or sharp knife, cut the dough round in half, then each half into quarters, and so on until you have 16 equal triangular pieces.
states.exit_condition: 16 evenly sized triangular wedges, each with a wide base at the outer edge of the circle and a narrow point at the center.

states.title: Roll Triangles into Crescents
states.direction: Starting at the base of a triangle, lightly roll up the dough so that the tip of the triangle tucks under the base of the cookie. Lightly push down to secure the shape. Place each rolled rugelach onto the parchment-lined baking sheet.
states.exit_condition: 16 rolled crescents arranged on the baking sheet with the tucked tip on the bottom. Spacing roughly 5cm apart so they don't merge during bake.

notes.text: Roll snug but not tight — over-tight rolls can split during baking. Tip tucked under the base prevents unrolling.

states.title: Freeze Shaped Rugelach
states.direction: Transfer the baking sheet to the freezer for 10-15 minutes to firm up the shapes before baking.
states.exit_condition: Rugelach are firm to the touch and hold their shape — well chilled but not frozen solid.

notes.text: The freeze step keeps the butter cold so the dough holds shape during the egg wash and the initial oven hit — critical for flake structure.

states.title: Egg Wash and Sugar
states.direction: Whisk the egg in a small bowl. Remove the baking sheet from the freezer. Brush each cookie with the egg wash, then sprinkle generously with granulated sugar.
states.exit_condition: Each cookie has a thin, even egg wash coating and a visible sugar dusting on top.

states.title: Bake
states.direction: Bake at 350°F (180°C) until golden brown and the base of each cookie is set and slightly darker than the tops, 20-25 minutes.
states.exit_condition: Tops are golden brown. Bottoms are set and slightly darker than the tops. Filling visible at the cut ends is bubbling slightly.

notes.text: Rotate sheet halfway through if your oven has hot spots — the front of the sheet often browns faster than the back.

reminders.prompt: How were the bottoms — pale, golden, or scorched?

methods.detail: Reheat at 300°F (150°C) on parchment-lined sheet for 5-7 minutes until warmed through and crust re-crisps. Avoid microwave — it makes the dough gummy.
300°F (150°C) for 4-5 minutes works well for 1-2 cookies at a time.

cook_log.summary: First bake — splash run, recipe-only. Food-processor dough came together well-hydrated; 1hr chill, shapes uneven. Bake stretched to ~30 min and bottoms set before tops browned. Flavor there, could be sweeter.
notes: Splash bake — going blind, recipe-only, learning pass
Kitchen pre-bake: 74.5°F ambient, 54% humidity
Used food processor for dough; also processed walnuts for filling. Order may matter — will think about it.
Dough seemed well-hydrated — never got the 'specks of loose flour' the recipe describes
Chilled ~1 hour (recipe allows 1hr or overnight)
Filling: walnut-currant per recipe
Rolled as single big disc → 16 pieces, none lost. Some shapes better than others.
Egg wash + sugar applied per recipe, then 10-15 min freezer
Baked ~30 min vs recipe's 22 min. Bottoms set before tops got golden brown.
Flavor present but could be sweeter — coarser sugar topping might help

photos.alt: Sheet pan of 16 freshly baked rugelach on parchment — blonde tops, set bottoms, walnut-currant filling leaked and caramelized between cookies. First-bake shape inconsistency visible: some tight crescents, others loose with filling exposed at the seam.

photos.alt: Finished rugelach packed into kraft paper bags with cellophane windows, on a dark wood table with the Tartine cookbook in the background. Bagged for sharing after the bake.

Try egg wash + sugar BEFORE freezer (Tartine does after)

Move bake to top rack to prevent bottoms setting before tops brown
Decide food processor order — dough first then walnuts, or reverse
Cross-check Claire Saffitz's almond paste rugelach recipe for technique cues

cook_log.summary: Second bake. 1hr chill, top rack helped browning but still needed ~35min (recipe says 22). Rolled tighter, look nicer. Flavor addicting. Effort/reward strong — viable scale-up.
notes: Dough into fridge ~11:26am CDT (approx, from "25 min ago").
Chilled 1 hour (not the 2hr try from last next_time).
Did not split into 2 discs — last bake's Claire-inspired split was for bigger batch, not needed at 16 count.
Kept egg wash + sugar after freezer (recipe order) — not switching to pre-freeze.
Used regular granulated sugar for topping — no demerara yet.
Top rack — helped browning.
Into oven 1:21pm CDT.
Out ~1:56pm CDT, ~35 min bake (~13 min over recipe's 22). Pastries reliably resist browning.
Food processor order: did dough first this time. Walnuts-first would rinse-out easier next bake.
Did not cross-reference Claire Saffitz this bake.
Rolling more diligent — crescents look nicer.
Flavor addicting, great. Solid effort/reward — candidate for scale-up / resell.

photos.alt: Sixteen finished crescents on a clear glass platter, arranged in loose rows. Pale gold — barely browned, confirming the recipe's reluctance to color even with +13 min over recipe time. Sugar topping glistens on tops. Currants escaped during shaping — scattered on the platter alongside the rolls. A few rolls show filling oozing from open ends; otherwise shapes are tighter and more uniform than last bake. Aesthetic: more disciplined rolling visible.
